correctness.rationale: Exact finite domain n=6,7,8,9,10. Even-scale Čech faces are exactly subsets of 2-vertex stars in K_n (Adams–Shukla–Singh Lemma 2.2). The delivered verifier enumerates every face (up to 5,673,836), pairs them by the defined ordered-coordinate matching, checks total pair coverage and fully topologically sorts all matched-lower V-path graphs. The generic matching is independently covered by Goyal–Shukla–Singh Proposition 3.1. Only the predicted critical three- and four-simplices survive; all signed integral Morse boundary coefficients vanish exactly, not merely modulo two. With no lower critical cells, π3 of the wedge 3-skeleton is H3 by Hurewicz, so every 4-cell attaches trivially. Matsushita Theorem 1.2 then yields the suspended bipartite-Kneser interpretation. Only the finite range has been verified; computations are not extrapolated into an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Statements and implications were compared against named source texts and exact graph constructions, including the standard acyclic matching lemma, ordinary Kneser KG(n,2), cyclic regular bipartite graph classes, bipartite Kneser edge ideals and the general closed-neighborhood suspension equivalence. They do not entail the five exact mixed-dimensional homotopy types for H(n,2). The known n=5 Desargues case is deliberately excluded. Novelty remains subject to an unindexed-equivalence risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent computation, thesis appendix or specialized bipartite Kneser topology result may exist. Searches alone are not novelty certificates.
The matching is standard; the original content is the exact critical-cell data, integral boundary and resulting five homotopy classifications.
No assertion is made for n >= 11; failure or success of the finite pattern beyond n=10 remains open here.

value.rationale: The ordinary Kneser graph and its bipartite double are natural combinatorial-topological objects. The first five cases above the separately known Desargues case admit a nontrivial two-degree wedge homotopy classification not determined by their graph order, regularity or edge-ideal linear-strand Betti numbers. The largest instance is a 90-vertex bipartite Kneser independence complex, computed via a 45-vertex triangular-graph Čech complex with 5,673,836 faces. These exact integral and homotopy data are mathematically motivated finite benchmark cases, not an arbitrary graph relabeling or a routine edge-ideal calculation. The incomplete n>=11 classification is disclosed.
